title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 94
paragraphs: As for Adeimantos, the Corinthian commander, the Athenians say that at the very start, when the ships were just engaging, struck by panic and terror he hoisted his sails and fled; and the Corinthians, seeing their flagship in flight, departed as well. The story goes on that when in their flight they came opposite the temple of Athena Skiras in the land of Salamis, a light vessel fell in with them by divine guidance — no one was ever found who had sent it — and it approached the Corinthians at a time when they knew nothing of what was happening with the fleet. From this it was inferred that the affair was of the Deity. When it drew near the ships, the men in the light vessel said: “Adeimantos, you have turned your ships away and set out in flight, deserting the Greek cause, while they are in fact winning a victory and getting the better of their foes just as they desired.” Since Adeimantos doubted them, they spoke a second time, offering themselves as hostages to be killed if the Greeks should prove not to be winning. Then he turned his ship back, he and the others with him, and they reached camp when the work was done. Such is the report the Athenians spread against them; but the Corinthians do not allow this, and maintain they were among the first in the sea-fight — and the rest of Greece also bears witness on their side.
